Cybersecurity Glossary

Attack Surface
The total set of points where an unauthorized user can try to enter or extract data.
Authentication
The process of verifying the identity of a user, device, or system.
Botnet
A network of compromised computers controlled remotely by an attacker.
CVE
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures, a catalog of publicly known security flaws.
CVSS
Common Vulnerability Scoring System, a standard for rating vulnerability severity.
CWE
Common Weakness Enumeration, a community list of software and hardware weakness types.
Encryption
Transforming readable data into ciphertext to protect its confidentiality.
Exploit
Code or a technique that takes advantage of a vulnerability to cause unintended behavior.
Firewall
A network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing traffic.
Hardening
Reducing a system's attack surface by removing unnecessary services and tightening configuration.
Honeypot
A decoy system designed to attract and study attackers.
Malware
Software written to harm, exploit, or otherwise compromise a system.
Patch
An update that corrects a security or functional defect in software.
Penetration Test
An authorized simulated attack used to evaluate the security of a system.
Phishing
A social-engineering attack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information.
Ransomware
Malware that encrypts data and demands payment for its release.
Remediation
The act of fixing or mitigating an identified vulnerability.
Threat Intelligence
Evidence-based knowledge about existing or emerging threats to assets.
Vulnerability
A weakness in a system that can be exploited to compromise security.
Zero Day
A vulnerability that is exploited before a patch is available.
Zero Trust
A security model that assumes no implicit trust and verifies every request.
SIEM
Security Information and Event Management, software that aggregates and analyzes security data.
